facts.statement: In 1975, Teresa Maryańska and Halszka Osmólska described the specimen as belonging to the genus Microceratops.
facts.quote: Four years later, in 1975, the specimen was described by Teresa Maryańska and Halszka Osmólska and referred to the genus Microceratops.

facts.statement: Paul Sereno later argued that the original genus Microceratops was a nomen dubium due to unjustified referrals and lack of diagnosis.
facts.quote: Paul Sereno noted that the referral for this specimen was injustified and overall, the genus lacked diagnosis, therefore, Microceratops (now named Microceratus) was considered a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: The name Graciliceratops means "slender horned face" and refers to the animal's fragile build.
facts.quote: The generic name, Graciliceratops, is derived from the Latin gracilis (meaning "slender") and the Greek keras (meaning "horn") and ops (meaning "face") in reference to its fragile build.

facts.statement: The holotype skull measures about 20 cm and unfused vertebrae suggest the individual was a juvenile when it died.
facts.quote: Although very damaged, the skull measures approximately 20 cm, the arches and centra of the sacral vertebrae are not fused, which indicates that this specimen was not fully grown when it died, probably a juvenile individual.

facts.statement: The juvenile specimen is estimated to be 60 cm long and weigh between 2.27 and 9.1 kg.
facts.quote: Its size is estimated at 60 cm long with a weight between 2.27 to 9.1 kg.

facts.statement: Adult Graciliceratops is estimated to have reached about 2 meters in length, similar to Protoceratops.
facts.quote: However, due to the immature nature of the specimen, the adult size is estimated around 2 m, or similar to Protoceratops.

facts.statement: The frill features large openings bounded by very slender struts, a structure similar to that of later Protoceratops.
facts.quote: The frill has large fenestrae bounded by very slender struts. This structure is very similar to that of the later Protoceratops.

facts.statement: The species is recognized by its fragile frill, a tibial-femoral ratio of 1.2:1, and well-developed squamosal processes.
facts.quote: Graciliceratops is recognised by the fragile frill and characteristic tibial-femoral ratio (1.2:1); the frill is also briefly elongated with well developed squamosal processes.

facts.statement: The femur measures 9.5 cm, is lightly curved with a large head, and has a fragile fourth trochanter located above the midlength.
facts.quote: The femur measures 9.5 cm, it is lightly curved and has a large head; the fourth trochanter is fragile and place above the midlength of the femoral end.

facts.statement: The tibia measures 11 cm, is larger than the femur, and has a more developed proximal articulation than distal.
facts.quote: Being larger than the femur, the tibia measures 11 cm and its proximal articulation is more developed than distally.

facts.statement: The toe claws are dorsoventrally flattened and somewhat sharply developed.
facts.quote: The pedal unguals are dorsoventrally flattened and somewhat sharply-developed.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis identifies Graciliceratops as a basal neoceratopsian.
facts.quote: Graciliceratops was found to be a basal neoceratopsian.

facts.statement: Graciliceratops is classified within the family Protoceratopsidae.
facts.quote: familia: Protoceratopsidae

facts.statement: Graciliceratops lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Graciliceratops (meaning "slender horned face") is a genus of neoceratopsian dinosaurs that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The animal lived approximately 90 million years ago during the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 90 millones de años, en el Turoniense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The Shireegiin Gashuun locality is likely from the early Late Cretaceous, older than the Djadokhta Formation where Protoceratops was found.
facts.quote: Se cree que la localidad de Shireegiin Gashuun es más antigua que las localidades de Djadokhta que produjeron Protoceratops , y probablemente sea de edad temprana del Cretácico tardío.

facts.statement: The time range for Graciliceratops is estimated from the Cenomanian to the Santonian, between 100.5 and 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Santonian (100.5 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Like other ceratopsians, Graciliceratops was likely a herbivore that used a powerful beak and cutting teeth to process tough plant matter.
facts.quote: Al igual que otros ceratopsianos, Graciliceratops habría sido un herbívoro, usando su poderoso pico y dientes cortantes para procesar la materia vegetal dura.

facts.statement: Because angiosperms were geographically limited during the Cretaceous, it is deduced that Graciliceratops fed on ferns, cycads, and conifers.
facts.quote: Durante el Cretácico, las plantas angiospermas estaban geográficamente limitadas, por lo que se deduce que el Graciliceratops se alimentaba de helechos, cícadas y coníferas.

facts.statement: The shape of its beak suggests it was used to bite leaves and thorns.
facts.quote: Por la forma de su pico se puede inferir que lo empleaba para morder las hojas y las espinas.

facts.statement: Fossilized fruits found in the formation suggest the existence of angiosperm plants in the environment.
facts.quote: Fossilized fruits have also been recovered from the upper and lower parts of the formation, suggesting the existence of Angiosperm plants.

facts.statement: Graciliceratops lived alongside diverse contemporaries including the dromaeosaurid Achillobator, tyrannosauroid Khankhuuluu, therizinosaurs, pachycephalosaurs, ornithomimosaurs, ankylosaurs, the sauropod Erketu, and the hadrosauroid Gobihadros.
facts.quote: It lived alongside other dinosaurs from the upper part, most notably the large dromaeosaurid Achillobator, the tyrannosauroid Khankhuuluu, therizinosaurs Erlikosaurus, Enigmosaurus, and Segnosaurus, the pachycephalosaur Amtocephale, the ornithomimosaur Garudimimus, the ankylosaurs Talarurus, Amtosaurus, Maleevus, and Tsagantegia, the large sauropod Erketu and the basal hadrosauroid Gobihadros.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the original classification of the specimen as Microceratops was valid, with Sereno considering it a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: Paul Sereno noted that the referral for this specimen was injustified and overall, the genus lacked diagnosis, therefore, Microceratops (now named Microceratus) was considered a nomen dubium.

rejected.statement: The holotype specimen of Graciliceratops was discovered in 1971 at the Sheeregeen Gashoon locality in the Bayan Shireh Formation of Mongolia.
rejected.quote: The holotype, ZPAL MgD-I/156, was discovered at the Bayan Shireh Formation in Mongolia, coming from the Sheeregeen Gashoon locality near Sainshand.

rejected.statement: Paul Sereno redescribed the specimen in 2000, establishing the new genus and species Graciliceratops mongoliensis.
rejected.quote: The referred specimen was redescribed by him, creating a new genus and species: Graciliceratops mongoliensis.

rejected.statement: Sediment types indicate Graciliceratops lived in a semiarid climate with rivers and large lakes.
rejected.quote: The presence of caliche, fluvial and lacustrine sediments, indicate a semiarid climate with rivers and large lakes around the zone.
